text:
maria: FYI, the e3d2f7 merge we rolled at 07:12 is causing a compile surge on canary — queue depth up, small-batch p95 token latency +25%.
ajay: saw that in dashboards too. any obvious fingerprint?
maria: quick findings: compile-controller shows repeated recompiles for the same kernel id, and KV cache eviction spikes right before. link: https://perf.redwood.internal/runs/2139 (flamegraph attached)
ken: that sounds like cache key churn. did e3d2f7 change kernel key shape?
maria: yes — it added batch_size into cache key to handle a batching heuristic edge. but it looks like the batching layer sometimes toggles batch_size for identical requests, causing cache misses and full recompile.
priya: ugh. So autotuner keeps picking a different kernel variant and triggers compile storms. CI perf tests flagged this?
ci-bot: CI perf check FAILED for canary-run e3d2f7 — compile latency regression +40% on short-seq small-batch benchmark. See: https://ci.redwood/in/2139/perf-report
ajay: can we reproduce locally? what commands to watch the behavior?
maria: repro steps: 
```
kubectl -n runtime logs deploy/compile-controller --tail=200
# watch the compile queue metric
curl http://canary-metrics.internal/compile_queue?window=5m
```
ken: also add `GODEBUG=gcshrinkstack=1`? jk. but seriously, I want a trace of the cache key values. can you drop a debug log of the key hashing?
maria: pushed a debug build to canary with KV_CACHE_DEBUG=1 — keys show: `model:v1|seq:128|batch:1` then `model:v1|seq:128|batch:2` for identical traffic because of a batching heuristic flip during pooling.
priya: sounds like a race in the batching aggregator. when it shrinks/expands a window we flip batch_size and that should not affect kernel identity. we should revert the cache key change ASAP.
ajay: agreed. options: 1) revert e3d2f7 2) hotfix to remove batch_size from key 3) gate the change behind a feature flag and roll back routing to previous canary.
ken: which is fastest? revert PR will take ~10m + CI, hotfix branch is similar. gating is quick if the flag exists. do we have a runtime gate?
maria: there is a runtime flag `kvcache.include_batch_size` — turned on by the merge. I can flip it to false for canary now.
priya: do it. Also let's start a quick bisect to find the minimal diff and add a unit test to prevent this regression.
maria: flipped flag to false at 07:42 — compile queue dropped ~70% within 2 minutes. p95 back to baseline.
ci-bot: rerun perf job queued.
ajay: great rollback plan. can we still merge a sanitized version that doesn't include batch_size or only includes it for models with non-deterministic batching?
ken: probably need to change batching aggregator to emit a canonical kernel_hint instead of raw batch size. that avoids toggles.
priya: I'll open a tracking ticket and a follow-up PR to add tests (batching aggregator determinism + kvcache key invariants).
maria: opened https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4723 "revert: remove batch_size from kvcache key (canary rollback)" — assigning @ken for follow-up.
ken: taking it. I'll also add a smoke test that fires identical requests and asserts identical cache keys across the aggregator boundary.
ajay: once the fix lands, let's run the full short-seq/small-batch perf suite before promoting.
maria: noted. thanks all :thumbsup:
buildbot: deploy canary rollback applied (deploy/compile-controller v1.66 -> v1.65).
ci-bot: PERF job for e3d2f7 (post-flag flip) shows regression cleared. PASS.
priya: closing the immediate rollout blocker. follow-ups: add tests, update changelog, and consider a small canary window before enabling any kvcache key shape changes.
maria: adding to eng-runtime retro for next week.
